clue.text: After wee dram there's a suspicion you'll see stars

parts.note: a peg is a small measure of spirits
sus is informal shorthand for suspicion

explanation.surface: A drinker has a nip of whisky and then starts seeing stars.
explanation.walkthrough: The stars the drinker sees are a real constellation, the winged horse.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to a large constellation in the northern sky, a group of stars.

clue.text: Course at Oxford includes old poet

indicators.note: includes means the old abbreviation sits within the course

parts.note: PPE, Philosophy, Politics and Economics, is a famous Oxford degree course

explanation.surface: A university course that has an aged poet on the reading list.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Pope was an eighteenth-century English poet.

clue.text: Marx and Mao making mother grumble

indicators.note: making turns the mother in the name into a grumble

parts.note: the name of the Chinese leader taken as written
ma is a mother
to grouch is to grumble

explanation.surface: Two famous communists drive a mother to complain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marx' suggests Karl, but it is the comedian brother.
explanation.definitionFit: Groucho was the most famous of the Marx Brothers comedy team.

clue.text: Delivering cuts regularly is "unkind", yes?

indicators.note: regularly asks for every other letter of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A question of whether handing out spending cuts is unkind.
explanation.definitionFit: Snide remarks are sneering and cutting, so the word describes someone delivering cuts.

clue.text: Chant about PM may be showing disrespect

indicators.note: about means the chant goes round the prime minister

parts.note: to chant is to sing
William Pitt was a British prime minister

explanation.surface: Football fans singing about the prime minister may be being rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Spitting at someone is a gesture of contempt, a way of showing disrespect.

clue.text: A runner's last in race — hit by javelin maybe!

indicators.note: in places the opening letter and the runner's final letter inside the word for race

parts.note: to race is to speed

indicators.note: last asks for the final letter of the word runner

explanation.surface: An athlete trailing last in a race is struck by a stray javelin at the sports meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A javelin is a kind of spear, so a person hit by one has been run through by a spear.

clue.text: Someone primarily kept on the gate?

definitions.text: Someone primarily kept on the gate?

indicators.note: primarily asks for the first letter of the word someone

parts.note: a gate is a way in, an entry

explanation.surface: A guard is kept posted at the gate.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry is a soldier posted to guard an entrance.

clue.text: Woman getting hold of her boy perhaps to eat a hot dish

indicators.note: getting hold of means the woman's name wraps around the rest

parts.note: Ena is a woman's name

indicators.note: to eat means the boy takes the letter a inside

parts.note: a boy is an example of a child

explanation.surface: A mother keeps hold of her son so he will eat a spicy meal.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a Mexican tortilla filled and baked in chilli sauce, a hot dish.

clue.text: Give girl massage for complaint

parts.note: to rub is to massage
Ella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Offering a girl a massage to ease an ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' is an illness, not a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubella, German measles, is a disease, and an illness is a complaint.

clue.text: What local Chiltern artist does perhaps to make connection

parts.note: an artist draws pictures
Tring is a town in the Chiltern Hills of Hertfordshire, England

explanation.surface: Asking what a painter from the Chilterns does to link things together.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawstring is a cord threaded through a hem that pulls and joins the edges.

clue.text: Not against seeing facilities

parts.note: pro means in favour of, not against
vision is the faculty of seeing

explanation.surface: Someone who is in favour of a scheme after viewing the amenities on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Provision is what is supplied or laid on for people's use, the amenities or facilities.

clue.text: Something with a hood that needs firm support

parts.note: Co is the standard abbreviation for company, a firm
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A hooded garment that has to be held up by something sturdy.
explanation.definitionFit: This venomous snake spreads the skin of its neck into a hood when threatened.

clue.text: See sports arenas offering comfortable seats

parts.note: Chester is a cathedral city and the seat of a bishop, a see
fields are grounds where games are played

explanation.surface: Go and look at the stadiums, which provide nice seating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb meaning look, but it is a bishop's see, here the English city of Chester.
explanation.definitionFit: These are deeply buttoned leather sofas, a classic kind of comfortable seat.

clue.text: They can provide uplift -—- sadness will shortly dissolve

indicators.note: dissolve means the letters break up and reform
shortly cuts the last letter off the word will

explanation.surface: Gloom will soon melt away, giving a lift to the spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims WILL to WIL, which joins SADNESS for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Windlasses are winches that wind rope to haul loads upwards, giving uplift.

clue.text: Smooth part of deal that comes with strict rule

parts.note: to iron is to smooth out creases
a hand is the set of cards a player receives in a deal

explanation.surface: A bit of a business agreement that arrives with tight regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deal' suggests business but is the dealing of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruling with an iron hand means governing harshly, so the phrase names strict control.

clue.text: The man on the road around China is an author

indicators.note: around means the man and the road wrap around the dynasty

parts.note: he is a pronoun for the man
a way is a road
Ming is a Chinese dynasty, also fine porcelain called china

explanation.surface: A man travelling through China turns out to be a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest Hemingway was an American novelist.

clue.text: Unknown group no longer drinking sitting in pub fair?

indicators.note: sitting in places the unknown and the group inside the word for pub

parts.note: a bar is a pub
z is a letter used for an unknown quantity in algebra
AA, Alcoholics Anonymous, is a group of people who have given up drinking

explanation.surface: A mysterious set of teetotallers sits in a tavern, which hardly seems fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A bazaar is a sale of goods, often for charity, much like a fete or fair.

clue.text: Fellow taken out as per contract

parts.note: a man is a fellow
dated means taken out on a date

explanation.surface: A man who has been escorted somewhere under the terms of an agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mandated is required by an official order, as an agreed contract stipulates.

clue.text: Leave a politician gets at end of year

parts.note: December, abbreviated Dec, is the final month of the year
MP stands for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A member of parliament receives something when the year finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to depart suddenly, so it is a verb for leave.

clue.text: Liquid for singers — litre to be drunk

indicators.note: to be drunk means the litre is swallowed into the word for singers

parts.note: choral means written for a choir

explanation.surface: A litre of something for the choir to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Chloral is a liquid compound used in making the sedative chloral hydrate.

clue.text: Sweet bit of food Bill found in desert

indicators.note: found in places the bill inside the word for desert

parts.note: to maroon is to abandon or desert someone
ac is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: Someone named Bill is discovered in a sandy waste eating a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' is the verb, to abandon, not the sandy place.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small almond biscuit, a sweet morsel to eat.

clue.text: Difficult individual to excite, being devoid of energy

parts.note: one is a single individual

indicators.note: being devoid of means the energy letter is taken away

parts.note: to rouse is to excite
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone hard to stir up because they lack energy.
explanation.definitionFit: An onerous task is burdensome and hard, so the word means difficult.

clue.text: Gloomy female replacing male in this bar

indicators.note: replacing means the female letter takes the place of the male one

parts.note: morbid means gloomy

explanation.surface: A sullen woman takes a man's place in this pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but is the verb, to prohibit.
explanation.definitionFit: To forbid something is to prohibit it, which is what bar means as a verb.

clue.text: Formula for putting together bits of galleon? Please be patient!

parts.words: Formula for putting together bits of galleon?
parts.note: the ship's name splits as G, ALL and EON: put the word all inside G, the abbreviation for good, then add an aeon, a long time

explanation.surface: Instructions for assembling a model ship, with a plea to be patient.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer read as an instruction builds the ship: ALL inside G (good), then EON (time).
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said to urge someone to wait, meaning it will happen eventually.

clue.text: "Children matter!" the head ejaculated

definitions.meaning: offspring, as in a man dying without heirs
a topic or question under discussion

explanation.surface: A headteacher exclaims that pupils are important.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue means offspring in legal language and also a subject under discussion.

clue.text: Brand of soap initially expensive, putting daughter off

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letter of the word soap
putting with off says the daughter letter is removed
off completes the instruction to take the daughter letter out

parts.note: dear means expensive

explanation.surface: A costly soap brand stops a daughter from buying it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brand' looks like a trade name but is the verb, to burn with a hot iron.
explanation.definitionFit: To brand is to burn a mark with hot iron, as to sear is to scorch.

clue.text: Lumpy bits put around trifle

indicators.note: put around means the word for lumpy bits is turned to face the other way

parts.note: warts are small lumpy growths on the skin

explanation.surface: Lumps of fruit are scattered over a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trifle' looks like the British layered pudding but means a thing of little worth; 'put around' turns WARTS back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of trivial value is said to be not worth a straw, so it is a trifle.

clue.text: Possible material for sculptor — pumice?

definitions.meaning: a cream limestone quarried near the English city of Bath, used in building and carving
a stone used in the bath to rub hard skin

explanation.surface: A sculptor wonders whether pumice would make a good medium.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumice is a stone kept by the bath for scrubbing, while the named limestone is a carving material.

clue.text: Turned out and took part in game, having joined the seconds

parts.note: played means took part in a game

explanation.surface: A player who appeared and joined the reserve team.
explanation.definitionFit: Feet that are splayed are turned outwards, so the word means turned out.

clue.text: For surgical assistant, vital being right behind doctor

indicators.note: behind puts the following pieces after the doctor

parts.note: esse is Latin for being, actual existence

explanation.surface: Vital for a surgeon's helper to be standing just to the right behind the doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A dresser is a hospital assistant who dresses wounds and helps a surgeon in theatre.
